subject: Game Theory
title: Deterrence Theory
description: A short lesson to help you apply Deterrence Theory.

hook.text: For 45 years, the US and USSR avoided nuclear war through a strategy called mutually assured destruction.

buildup.text: Deterrence works by threatening retaliation so devastating that attack becomes irrational.

discovery.text: The key requirement: second-strike capability. You must be able to retaliate even after being attacked first.

twist.text: Deterrence requires appearing slightly irrational—enemies must believe you'd actually follow through on destruction.

climax.text: Schelling called this the 'threat that leaves something to chance'—even leaders can't fully control escalation.

punchline.text: Peace through the promise of destruction.

quiz.question: What is essential for nuclear deterrence to work?
